script.title: Offer vs Invitation to Offer
script.caption_hook: A price tag is not a promise to sell. Here's why.

lines.say: Wait, a price tag on a shirt isn't a promise to sell?
Good question! Let's compare an offer with an invitation to offer.

board.title: Offer or Invitation?
board.sub: Price tag is not a promise

lines.say: So what exactly is an offer, Ma'am?
An offer shows willingness to do something, made to get the other's assent, and ready to be bound.
Okay, and what happens once it's accepted?
Acceptance turns the offer into a promise, an agreement. It becomes a contract only if it is enforceable by law.

board.title: Offer accepted
board.sub: Agreement; a contract if enforceable by law

lines.say: Then what's an invitation to offer?
It only invites offers, so it can't be accepted.
So why isn't a price tag an offer?
Then the shopkeeper would be bound to sell to everyone, even for a wrong tag or no stock.
Oh! So I make the offer at the counter?
Yes! You carry the item to the counter. That's your offer. The cashier accepts by billing it.
A reward ad for anyone who performs a condition is a general offer. Performing it is acceptance.
Remember: the shop invites, you offer!

check_notes: Writer: Line 6 and its board now follow Sections 2(b), 2(e), 2(h): acceptance makes a promise/agreement, a contract only if enforceable by law. Line 4 board reworded to "Made to get their assent" (Section 2(a)). Line 8 says an invitation "can't be accepted"; tender and auction bids are not covered, to keep it simple.

Checker: Line 4 (voice and board 'Willing to do something'): Section 2(a) of the Indian Contract Act defines a proposal as showing willingness 'to do or to abstain from doing' something, with a view to obtaining the other person's assent. The script leaves out 'abstain from doing'. Correct version: 'An offer shows willingness to do or not do something, made to get the other's assent.' The board line should read 'Willing to do or abstain'.

Checker: Line 6 board formula 'Acceptance = promise': this is imprecise. Under Section 2(b), it is the proposal, once accepted, that becomes a promise. Acceptance itself is not the promise. Correct version: 'Offer + Acceptance = Promise (Agreement)'. The voice line already says this correctly ('Acceptance turns the offer into a promise').
